incidents.what_happened: Issue #156 used an unbalanced pattern in a jq test() filter. Fixtures reached it only when one specific history entry existed, so ordinary coverage missed the syntax error.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #156 was fixed in commit 22e253d with a scheduler regression case; the pattern can be compiled directly with jq.
incidents.classic_pattern: A data-dependent fixture leaves a literal regular expression uncompiled until one exact branch is selected.
incidents.best_known_solution: Compile every literal jq test(), match(), capture(), sub() and gsub() pattern in engine shell files with jq before relying on fixture execution.
options_considered: Add a fixture for the known history entry; this would cover one branch but leave other literal patterns dependent on fixture data.
Compile every literal regex with jq itself; this covers syntax independently of runtime data and was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Every literal jq regex in engine shell files compiles successfully.

machine_checks.why: Compiles engine literals and proves an unbalanced planted pattern is rejected.
Retains the original scheduler regression case.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157 cached candidate rows containing issue bodies by passing the complete string to jq through --arg. A large intake exceeded the OS argument limit and failed with Argument list too long.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #157 was fixed in commit e4a748c by streaming the cache rows; scheduler.test.sh adds a fixture over 2 MiB.
incidents.classic_pattern: A growing list or body is bound as one jq argv value; per-argument limits can be exceeded before the program starts.
incidents.best_known_solution: Stream large JSON or prose through stdin or a file, and lint known-unbounded variable names passed to --arg or --argjson.
options_considered: Truncate issue bodies; this loses cache data and does not bound row counts.
Split the cache into multiple argv chunks; this keeps the same fragile transport contract.
Stream the serialized value to jq and flag --arg/--argjson bindings of known unbounded variables; this avoids argv limits and follows the existing lint style, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: A rows variable passed through --arg is flagged; fixed stdin streaming passes.

machine_checks.why: Proves a planted --arg rows "$rows" binding is flagged and scans production shell files.
Exercises the #159 large-row cache regression above 2 MiB.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157's refill path read HANDOFF_PR_CENSUS before assignment under set -u, aborting a tick before existing startable work was dispatched.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The fix from branch fix/refill-census-unbound merged in pull request #160 as commit c9cb023.
incidents.classic_pattern: A fallback path skips a path-local assignment and later reads an unset variable under nounset.
incidents.best_known_solution: Initialize the census before refill or fallback reads and keep nounset enabled.
options_considered: Disable nounset for the fallback; this suppresses the useful error and lets missing state flow onward.
Initialize the census before every path can read it; this preserves nounset and gives fallback logic a defined empty state, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Refill completes and existing startable work dispatches despite the handoff lookup path.

machine_checks.why: Regression case reaches the refill fallback with set -u and checks dispatch continues.

incidents.what_happened: One gh pr list call hung for 44 minutes until TICK-TIMEOUT; refill remained locked out for 28 minutes.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The scheduler wrapper called command gh without a timeout; the bounded-wrapper fix is on branch fix/scheduler-gh-timeout.
incidents.classic_pattern: An unbounded network CLI call can keep a scheduler lock longer than the useful work window.
incidents.best_known_solution: Route scheduler gh() through gh_timeout with a validated per-call limit, log timed-out calls, and statically reject direct command gh calls in scheduler and library sources.
options_considered: Raise TICK-TIMEOUT; this lengthens the maximum lockout rather than bounding each network call.
Retry a stalled command; without a deadline this repeats the same unbounded wait.
Use one bounded timeout wrapper for scheduler GitHub calls and fail static checks on direct command gh bypasses; this constrains each call and prevents callsite drift, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: No production scheduler/lib shell source calls command gh directly.

machine_checks.why: Checks all scheduler/lib shell sources and proves a planted command gh bypass is rejected.
Times out a stalled gh CLI call, verifies the child is stopped, and checks timeout logging.

incidents.what_happened: A product-pin rollback was refused by publish preflight with resolved-config-check: CHANGED, leaving a broken engine live.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The preflight did not recognize the explicit rollback path; the engine-swap canary fix is on branch feat/engine-swap-canary.
incidents.classic_pattern: A broad safety preflight blocks a narrowly authorized recovery change because the recovery path is not modeled as an allowed transition.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep ordinary changed-config checks, while allowing only an explicit verified engine-swap/canary path to carry the product pin change.
options_considered: Skip preflight for every rollback; this would permit unrelated resolved-config drift.
Leave the old engine live until a fresh forward release is ready; this prolongs a known-broken state.
Require a verified engine-swap path for the pin change while preserving ordinary refusal behavior; this keeps the gate and supports controlled recovery, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: The verified swap/rollback case passes while unlisted resolved-config changes remain blocked.

machine_checks.why: Exercises engine version selection and publish preflight behavior.
Keeps the default refusal for unlisted resolved-config changes and accepts listed changes with a reason.
